<p> Certain infectious and parasitic diseases A00-B99 > </p>
<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>
<p> code to identify resistance to antimicrobial drugs ( </p>
<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as A00-B99. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>
<p> certain localized infections - see body system-related chapters </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (A00-B99) and the excluded code together. </p>

<p> Sequelae of infectious and parasitic diseases </p>
<p> Code First </p>
<p> condition resulting from (sequela) the infectious or parasitic disease </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Categories B90-B94 are to be used to indicate conditions in categories A00-B89 as the cause of sequelae, which are themselves classified elsewhere. The 'sequelae' include conditions specified as such; they also include residuals of diseases classifiable to the above categories if there is evidence that the disease itself is no longer present. Codes from these categories are not to be used for chronic infections. Code chronic current infections to active infectious disease as appropriate. </p>

<p> Sequelae of infectious and parasitic diseases B90-B94 > </p>
<p> Sequelae of infectious and parasitic diseases </p>
<p> Code First </p>
<p> condition resulting from (sequela) the infectious or parasitic disease </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Categories B90-B94 are to be used to indicate conditions in categories A00-B89 as the cause of sequelae, which are themselves classified elsewhere. The 'sequelae' include conditions specified as such; they also include residuals of diseases classifiable to the above categories if there is evidence that the disease itself is no longer present. Codes from these categories are not to be used for chronic infections. Code chronic current infections to active infectious disease as appropriate. </p>
<p> Cholera </p>
<p> Unspecified parasitic disease </p>
<p> as the cause of sequelae, which are themselves classified elsewhere. The 'sequelae' include conditions specified as such; they also include residuals of diseases classifiable to the above categories if there is evidence that the disease itself is no longer present. Codes from these categories are not to be used for chronic infections. Code chronic current infections to active infectious disease as appropriate. </p>
<p> Code First </p>
<p> Code First Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions, ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>

<p> Neoplasms C00-D49 > </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Functional activity </p>
<p> All neoplasms are classified in this chapter, whether they are functionally active or not. An additional code from Chapter 4 may be used, to identify functional activity associated with any neoplasm. </p>
<p> Morphology [Histology] </p>
<p> Chapter 2 classifies neoplasms primarily by site (topography), with broad groupings for behavior, malignant, in situ, benign, etc. The Table of Neoplasms should be used to identify the correct topography code. In a few cases, such as for malignant melanoma and certain neuroendocrine tumors, the morphology (histologic type) is included in the category and codes. </p>
<p> Primary malignant neoplasms overlapping site boundaries </p>
<p> A primary malignant neoplasm that overlaps two or more contiguous (next to each other) sites should be classified to the subcategory/code .8 ('overlapping lesion'), unless the combination is specifically indexed elsewhere. For multiple neoplasms of the same site that are not contiguous, such as tumors in different quadrants of the same breast, codes for each site should be assigned. </p>
<p> Malignant neoplasm of ectopic tissue </p>
<p> Malignant neoplasms of ectopic tissue are to be coded to the site mentioned, e.g., ectopic pancreatic malignant neoplasms are coded to pancreas, unspecified ( </p>
<p> Neoplasms of uncertain behavior, polycythemia vera and myelodysplastic syndromes </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Categories D37-D44, and D48 classify by site neoplasms of uncertain behavior, i.e., histologic confirmation whether the neoplasm is malignant or benign cannot be made. </p>

<p> Malignant neoplasms of digestive organs C15-C26 > </p>
<p> Type 1 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 1 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as C15-C26. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>
<p> Kaposi's sarcoma of gastrointestinal sites ( </p>
<p> ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Code C46.4 </p>
<p> Kaposi's sarcoma of gastrointestinal sites </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (C15-C26) and the excluded code together. </p>

<p> This block comprises a range of mental disorders grouped together on the basis of their having in common a demonstrable etiology in cerebral disease, brain injury, or other insult leading to cerebral dysfunction. The dysfunction may be primary, as in diseases, injuries, and insults that affect the brain directly and selectively; or secondary, as in systemic diseases and disorders that attack the brain only as one of the multiple organs or systems of the body that are involved. </p>
<p> Anxiety, dissociative, stress-related, somatoform and other nonpsychotic mental disorders </p>
<p> Behavioral syndromes associated with physiological disturbances and physical factors </p>
<p> Behavioral and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Codes within categories F90-F98 may be used regardless of the age of a patient. These disorders generally have onset within the childhood or adolescent years, but may continue throughout life or not be diagnosed until adulthood </p>
<p> Intellectual disabilities F70-F79 > </p>
<p> Code First </p>
<p> Code First Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions, ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>
<p> any associated physical or developmental disorders </p>
<p> Type 1 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 1 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as F70-F79. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>

<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (G00-G99) and the excluded code together. </p>

<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>

<p> Cerebrovascular diseases I60-I69 > </p>
<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>

<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (M00-M99) and the excluded code together. </p>

<p> Infectious arthropathies </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> This block comprises arthropathies due to microbiological agents. Distinction is made between the following types of etiological relationship: </p>
<p> a) direct infection of joint, where organisms invade synovial tissue and microbial antigen is present in the joint; </p>
<p> b) indirect infection, which may be of two types: a reactive arthropathy, where microbial infection of the body is established but neither organisms nor antigens can be identified in the joint, and a postinfective arthropathy, where microbial antigen is present but recovery of an organism is inconstant and evidence of local multiplication is lacking. </p>

<p> Type 1 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 1 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as M26-M27. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>

<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (N00-N99) and the excluded code together. </p>

<p> Legal blindness, as defined in USA </p>
<p> 2016 2017 2018 2019 Billable/Specific Code </p>
<p> Applicable To </p>
<p> Blindness NOS according to USA definition </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> The table below gives a classification of severity of visual impairment recommended by a WHO Study Group on the Prevention of Blindness, Geneva, 6-10 November 1972. </p>
<p> The term 'low vision' in category H54 comprises categories 1 and 2 of the table, the term 'blindness' categories 3, 4 and 5, and the term 'unqualified visual loss' category 9. </p>
<p> If the extent of the visual field is taken into account, patients with a field no greater than 10 but greater than 5 around central fixation should be placed in category 3 and patients with a field no greater than 5 around central fixation should be placed in category 4, even if the central acuity is not impaired. </p>
<p> Type 1 Excludes </p>
<p> legal blindness with specification of impairment level (H54.0-H54.7) </p>

<p> Activity codes </p>

<p> Note </p>
<p> Category Y93 is provided for use to indicate the activity of the person seeking healthcare for an injury or health condition, such as a heart attack while shoveling snow, which resulted from, or was contributed to, by the activity. These codes are appropriate for use for both acute injuries, such as those from chapter 19, and conditions that are due to the long-term, cumulative effects of an activity, such as those from chapter 13. They are also appropriate for use with external cause codes for cause and intent if identifying the activity provides additional information on the event. These codes should be used in conjunction with codes for external cause status (Y99) and place of occurrence (Y92). </p>

<p> Activity codes </p>
<p> 2016 2017 2018 2019 Non-Billable/Non-Specific Code </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Category Y93 is provided for use to indicate the activity of the person seeking healthcare for an injury or health condition, such as a heart attack while shoveling snow, which resulted from, or was contributed to, by the activity. These codes are appropriate for use for both acute injuries, such as those from chapter 19, and conditions that are due to the long-term, cumulative effects of an activity, such as those from chapter 13. They are also appropriate for use with external cause codes for cause and intent if identifying the activity provides additional information on the event. These codes should be used in conjunction with codes for external cause status (Y99) and place of occurrence (Y92). </p>

<p> Pregnancy, childbirth and the puerperium O00-O9A > </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> CODES FROM THIS CHAPTER ARE FOR USE ONLY ON MATERNAL RECORDS, NEVER ON NEWBORN RECORDS </p>
<p> Codes from this chapter are for use for conditions related to or aggravated by the pregnancy, childbirth, or by the puerperium (maternal causes or obstetric causes) </p>
<p> Trimesters are counted from the first day of the last menstrual period. They are defined as follows: </p>
<p> 1st trimester- less than 14 weeks 0 days </p>
<p> 2nd trimester- 14 weeks 0 days to less than 28 weeks 0 days </p>
<p> 3rd trimester- 28 weeks 0 days until delivery </p>
<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>

<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (Q00-Q99) and the excluded code together. </p>

<p> Cleft lip and cleft palate Q35-Q37 > </p>
<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>
<p> code to identify associated malformation of the nose ( </p>
<p> ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Code Q30.2 </p>
<p> Fissured, notched and cleft nose </p>
<p> 2016 2017 2018 2019 Billable/Specific Code POA Exempt </p>
<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as Q35-Q37. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>

<p> Other specified symptoms and signs involving the circulatory and respiratory systems </p>
<p> Symptoms, signs and abnormal clinical and laboratory findings, not elsewhere classified R00-R99 > </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> This chapter includes symptoms, signs, abnormal results of clinical or other investigative procedures, and ill-defined conditions regarding which no diagnosis classifiable elsewhere is recorded. </p>
<p> Signs and symptoms that point rather definitely to a given diagnosis have been assigned to a category in other chapters of the classification. In general, categories in this chapter include the less well-defined conditions and symptoms that, without the necessary study of the case to establish a final diagnosis, point perhaps equally to two or more diseases or to two or more systems of the body. Practically all categories in the chapter could be designated 'not otherwise specified', 'unknown etiology' or 'transient'. The Alphabetical Index should be consulted to determine which symptoms and signs are to be allocated here and which to other chapters. The residual subcategories, numbered .8, are generally provided for other relevant symptoms that cannot be allocated elsewhere in the classification. </p>
<p> The conditions and signs or symptoms included in categories </p>
<p> ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Code R00 </p>
<p> Abnormalities of heart beat </p>
<p> 2016 2017 2018 2019 Non-Billable/Non-Specific Code </p>
<p> Abnormal results of function studies </p>
<p> (a) cases for which no more specific diagnosis can be made even after all the facts bearing on the case have been investigated; </p>
<p> (b) signs or symptoms existing at the time of initial encounter that proved to be transient and whose causes could not be determined; </p>
<p> (c) provisional diagnosis in a patient who failed to return for further investigation or care; </p>
<p> (d) cases referred elsewhere for investigation or treatment before the diagnosis was made; </p>
<p> (e) cases in which a more precise diagnosis was not available for any other reason; </p>
<p> (f) certain symptoms, for which supplementary information is provided, that represent important problems in medical care in their own right. </p>

<p> Code Also </p>
<p> Code Also Help </p>
<p> A code also note instructs that 2 codes may be required to fully describe a condition but the sequencing of the two codes is discretionary, depending on the severity of the conditions and the reason for the encounter. </p>
<p> for any associated infection </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (S00-S09) and the excluded code together. </p>
<p> burns and corrosions ( </p>
<p> ICD-10-CM Diagnosis Code T20 </p>
<p> Burn and corrosion of head, face, and neck </p>
<p> 2016 2017 2018 2019 Non-Billable/Non-Specific Code </p>

<p> Toxic effect of venom of other arthropods </p>
<p> "Includes" further defines, or give examples of, the content of the code or category. </p>
<p> Injury, poisoning and certain other consequences of external causes S00-T88 > </p>
<p> Note </p>
<p> Use secondary code(s) from Chapter 20, External causes of morbidity, to indicate cause of injury. Codes within the T section that include the external cause do not require an additional external cause code </p>
<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>
<p> code to identify any retained foreign body, if applicable ( </p>
<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as S00-T88. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>

<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>

<p> Use Additional </p>
<p> Use Additional Help </p>
<p> Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology. For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation. Wherever such a combination exists there is a "use additional code" note at the etiology code, and a "code first" note at the manifestation code. These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation. In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, "in diseases classified elsewhere." Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code. "In diseases classified elsewhere" codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principle diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition. </p>
<p> code(s): </p>

<p> A type 1 excludes note is a pure excludes. It means "not coded here". A type 1 excludes note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as T51-T65. A type 1 excludes note is for used for when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition. </p>

<p> (a) When a person who may or may not be sick encounters the health services for some specific purpose, such as to receive limited care or service for a current condition, to donate an organ or tissue, to receive prophylactic vaccination (immunization), or to discuss a problem which is in itself not a disease or injury. </p>

<p> Type 2 Excludes </p>
<p> Type 2 Excludes Help </p>
<p> A type 2 excludes note represents "not included here". A type 2 excludes note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time. When a type 2 excludes note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code (Z40-Z53) and the excluded code together. </p>
